newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTZ-CRA says iron project goes ahead.
newsitem.headline: RTZ-CRA says iron project goes ahead.

text.p: RTZ Plc-CRA Ltd said on Wednesday it had reached an agreement with the Gumala Aboriginal Corp which paved the way for the A$500 million development of the Yandicoogina iron ore mine in Western Australia.

The Anglo-Australian mining house said the agreement by its unit Hamersley Iron is the first regional land use agreement for a major resource project to be concluded since the Mabo decision in Australia's High Court.
"While negotiations initially commenced outside the ambit of Native Title Act, the agreement was concluded under the umbrella of the Act," RTZ-CRA said.

RTZ-CRA said the Pilbara agreement lays the foundation for a collaborative long-term relationship between Gumala and Hamersley in which the Bunjima, Niapali and Innawonga groups represented by Gumala will receive a benefits package linked to the success of the Yandicoogina project, near Newman.

Under the agreement, Hamersley Iron will make contributions over the life of the Yandicoogina mines to trusts established to fund long-term community benefits to all Aboriginal people with traditional ties to the area, the group said.
It said the value of benefits to the aboriginal community could exceed A$60 million over 20 years.
At 2.45 p.m. (0345 GMT), CRA shares were 18 cents up at A$18.48 with more than 700,000 shares traded.
